user.title: RF Device Manager
user.description: Create a new RF device or duplicate an existing one.

create_device.title: Create new RF device
create_device.description: Define the RF device. {transmitter_count} RF transmitter(s) were found. Codes are learned afterwards via the device options (Configure).

data_description.name: Shown as the device name in Home Assistant.
data_description.transmitter: The radio_frequency entity (e.g. an ESPHome IR/RF proxy) used to send codes for this device.
data_description.frequency_preset: Carrier frequency of the device's remote control.
data_description.frequency_custom: Only used when 'Custom frequency…' is selected above.
data_description.default_repeat: How many extra times commands are repeated when sending. 0 sends once; 7 (default) matches a short button press.

duplicate_device.title: Duplicate device
duplicate_device.description: All codes of the selected device are copied to the new device.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure {name}
reconfigure.description: Adjust the base settings of this RF device.

error.no_transmitters: No RF transmitters found. Add an ESPHome node with the ir_rf_proxy radio_frequency platform (or other radio_frequency hardware) first.
error.transmitter_not_found: This transmitter entity does not exist (anymore).
error.unsupported_frequency: The selected transmitter does not support this frequency.
error.frequency_required: Please enter a custom frequency in Hz.

abort.no_devices: There is no device to duplicate yet.

init.title: Manage RF device
init.description: Manage settings and RF codes of this device.

add_code.title: New RF code
add_code.description: Step 1 – name the code and choose which entity it should become. You will then learn or enter its commands one by one.

type_settings.title: Configure {entity_type}
type_settings.description: Step 2 – options for “{code_name}”. They determine which commands are learned next.

slot_menu.title: Provide command
slot_menu.description:
Step {position} for “{code_name}” – provide the command **{slot}**.

Available RF receivers: {receivers}

slot_learn_failed.title: No signal received
slot_learn_failed.description:
No RF signal was received for **{slot}** ({position}). Check that a receiver is in range.

Available RF receivers: {receivers}

slot_no_receiver.title: No RF receiver available

slot_learn_done.title: Select signal

slot_manual.title: Manual entry: {slot}
slot_manual.description: Enter the RF data for **{slot}** ({position}). Fill only the field matching the chosen format.

manage_codes.title: Manage RF codes
manage_codes.description: Select the RF code to manage.

code_view.title: RF code details

code_relearn.title: Learn command again
code_relearn.description: Which command of “{code_name}” do you want to learn again?

code_test.title: Test command
code_test.description: Which command of “{code_name}” should be sent?

code_delete.title: Delete RF code
code_delete.description: Delete “{code_name}” ({entity_type})? The entity and all learned commands will be removed permanently.

error.invalid_options: Please enter at least one unique option.
error.invalid_values: Please enter valid, comma separated values.
error.invalid_timings: The timings could not be parsed.
error.too_few_pulses: The signal is too short to be a valid RF code.
error.invalid_tristate: Tri-state codes may only contain 0, 1 and F.
error.invalid_binary: Binary codes may only contain 0 and 1.
error.invalid_pronto: The Pronto code could not be parsed.
error.invalid_b0: The Tasmota RfRaw code could not be parsed. Expected AA B0 … 55.
error.transmitter_not_found: This transmitter entity does not exist (anymore).
error.unsupported_frequency: The selected transmitter does not support this frequency.
error.frequency_required: Please enter a custom frequency in Hz.

abort.no_codes: This device has no RF codes yet.

send_code.name: Send code
send_code.description: Sends a stored command of a managed RF device.

code.name: RF code
code.description: Name or ID of the RF code.

command.name: Command
command.description: Command slot (e.g. on, off, open). Defaults to the first configured command.

repeat.name: Repeats
repeat.description: Extra repetitions (0 = send once); overrides the stored value.

send_raw.name: Send raw RF data
send_raw.description: Transmits ad-hoc RF data through a radio_frequency transmitter.

transmitter.name: Transmitter
transmitter.description: The radio_frequency entity to send with.

timings.name: Raw timings
timings.description: Signed microsecond timings (JSON array or separated numbers).

b0_code.name: Tasmota RfRaw code
b0_code.description: Tasmota/Portisch RfRaw B0 or B1 bucket code (AA B0 … 55).

tristate_code.name: Tri-state code
tristate_code.description: PT2262/EV1527 style code consisting of 0, 1 and F.

binary_code.name: Binary code
binary_code.description: Bit string encoded with the selected rc-switch protocol.

pulse_length.name: Pulse length
pulse_length.description: Base pulse length in µs for tri-state/binary codes.

repeat.name: Repeats
repeat.description: Extra repetitions of the transmission (0 = send once).

learn_code.name: Learn code
learn_code.description: Listens for RF signals and returns the captured, analyzed codes as response data.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long to wait for the first signal (seconds).

init.title: Select replacement transmitter
init.description: The transmitter `{transmitter}` used by “{name}” no longer exists. Choose a replacement.

empty_command.message: This RF command contains no timing data.

device_not_found.message: No managed RF device found for “{device_id}”.

code_not_found.message: RF code “{code}” was not found on this device.

no_rf_data.message: Provide raw timings, a tri-state/binary code or a Pronto code.
